findings.summary: refute.js — the very stage this REFUTE call is running as — trusts the caller-supplied `stageOutputs` object (ground/design/hiddenDecisionScan) with a shape-only check and never reads, hashes, or otherwise authenticates it against the on-disk run record. This exact gap was surfaced by this run's own round-6 hidden-decision-scan as an unresolved, high-severity forced choice, and the contract was never updated to address it.
findings.evidence: hidden-decision-output-round6.json finding #1 (severity: high): 'refute.js validates only the SHAPE of stageOutputs.ground/.design/.hiddenDecisionScan via __stageResultContracts({operation:'validate'}) and never re-reads the stage's own persisted run-record file, hashes it, or compares it to anything.' I independently confirmed this against live code: `grep -n "hash\|digest\|readFile.*ground\|readFile.*design\|stageOutputs" .agents/workflows/refute.js` shows refute.js:1185-1244 takes `stageOutputs[name]` straight from the input and passes it to `__stageResultContracts` for shape validation only — no fs read of a run-record path, no digest, no disk comparison anywhere in the file. `grep -n "hash\|read-back\|readback\|unauthenticated\|authenticat" .dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/contract.md` returns zero matches — none of the hidden-decision-scan's four options (trust-and-document / read-back / hash-anchor / Lie-catcher-diffs-against-disk) is recorded as chosen. `stat -f "%Sm" contract.md` = Sep 2 18:48:30; `stat -f "%Sm" hidden-decision-output-round6.json` = Sep 2 18:59:35 — the scan that raised this finding ran 11 minutes after the contract's last edit, and `ls -la -t` on the run-record directory shows that scan output is the most-recently-touched file in the whole directory, i.e. nothing addressed it afterward. This directly violates rails-run-a-workflow's own rule: 'No contract advances past CONTRACT with an unresolved forced choice.'
findings.fix: Get Tim's explicit decision on one of the hidden-decision-scan's options for refute.js's stageOutputs trust boundary (or an equivalent), record it verbatim in the contract's Decisions section, and implement it in refute.js (and the required-agent-runtime / stage-result-contracts copied blocks as needed) before this run is treated as gate-ready. If Tim explicitly accepts caller-trust as sufficient, that acceptance must be a recorded decision with his words, not a silent default.

Contract's `copied-module-convention` section (contract.md lines ~199-207) names only the inprocess path as the retired-originals location and contains no header-rewrite or permanent-location plan. Ground fact (rail-ownership area) confirms the live header text, e.g. `architecture.js:11` reads 'Generated copy of .dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/retired-workflow-modules/workflow-input.js.' rails-run-a-workflow SKILL.md Provenance section states: 'Move the run record to `.dev/completed/run-records/` inside the same shipping pull request, before merge.' `grep -n "permanent\|completed/run-records.*header\|rewrite.*header\|header.*rewrite" .dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/contract.md` returns zero matches. findings.summary: architecture.js is excluded from the `stage-result-contracts` single owner that this same reorganization established for every other stage's author-output schema/validation and final self-check, giving that one invariant a second, unsynchronized implementation — SOLID Violation #1 (no single owner) and #4 (unjustified second path).
findings.evidence: The contract's own Reuse ledger (contract.md:506) states the ruling for this exact capability: "Stage result schemas and their validation had diverging copies across the stage scripts. One authored source owns them, delivered under copied-module-convention inside the stage-result-contracts block." Live-code re-check: `grep -c __stageResultContracts .agents/workflows/architecture.js` = 0 — architecture.js never calls the shared block at all. The shared switch inside `stage-result-contracts` (present byte-identical in ground.js/design.js/hidden-decision-scan.js/implement.js/prior-art-ledger.js/refute.js/rule-phase.js/tdd.js, confirmed via `node eng/check-copied-modules.mjs` -> 'stage-result-contracts 8 copies identical') defines exactly these `case` names: ground-facts, prior-art-candidates, prior-art-verdict, design-proposal, design-verdict, hidden-candidates, hidden-findings, rule-phase-author, tdd-author, ground-stage, prior-art-stage, design-stage, hidden-decision-stage, rule-phase-stage, tdd-stage — there is no `architecture-author` or `architecture-stage` case anywhere (`grep -rn 'architecture-author|architecture-stage' .agents/workflows/*.js` -> hits only inside architecture.js's own inline role-id string, never inside the shared block). Instead architecture.js:599-624 defines its own standalone `SKELETON_SCHEMA` plus an ad hoc inline `validation:{...}` object (architecture.js:697-717) and hands them straight to `__requiredAgentRuntime`, bypassing the shared owner. It also never self-checks its own final result: every sibling stage that participates in the shared owner ends with `await __stageResultContracts({name:'<x>-stage', operation:'validate', result})` (ground.js:1413, design.js:1306, hidden-decision-scan.js:1331, rule-phase.js:1355-1361, tdd.js:1415-1421) — architecture.js's tail (last ~60 lines, `return { skeletonFiles: author.skeletonFiles, ... }`) has no equivalent call. I tested and refuted the theory that this is a principled boundary (e.g. 'only results consumed by a later script need the shared owner'): implement.js's args destructure (implement.js:1206-1221) has no `architectureResult` field at all, so ARCHITECTURE's result genuinely is never cross-consumed — but `prior-art-candidates`/`prior-art-verdict` are ALSO never consumed by any later script (used only inside ground.js's own inlined `__priorArtLedger`) and are still registered in the shared switch with a `prior-art-stage` self-check, disproving any cross-consumption carve-out. No comment in architecture.js, the contract, or the retired provenance file `.dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/retired-workflow-modules/stage-result-contracts.js` (`grep -n architecture` on that file -> no hits) states a reason ARCHITECTURE cannot be owned by the same mechanism the contract says already owns this invariant 'across the stage scripts.'
findings.fix: Add an `architecture-author` case (the existing `SKELETON_SCHEMA` plus its current validation rules) and an `architecture-stage` case (the existing `required` field list) to the shared `stage-result-contracts` switch, applied identically to all 8 copies so `eng/check-copied-modules.mjs` still reports them byte-identical; then change architecture.js to fetch its author schema/validation via `__stageResultContracts({name:'architecture-author', ...})` the same way rule-phase.js and tdd.js fetch theirs, and to end with `await __stageResultContracts({name:'architecture-stage', operation:'validate', result})` before returning — removing the standalone inline `SKELETON_SCHEMA` and ad hoc validation object so ARCHITECTURE's result contract has the same single owner as every other stage.

refutationAttempts: Checked whether ARCHITECTURE's exclusion from `stage-result-contracts` is justified because, unlike RULE-PHASE/TDD (consumed by implement.js) and GROUND/DESIGN/hidden-decision-scan (consumed by refute.js), its result is never passed as a structured, validated input into any later script — confirmed true (implement.js has no `architectureResult` field), but refuted as a justification because `prior-art-candidates`/`prior-art-verdict`, which are likewise never cross-consumed by a later script (used only inside ground.js's own inlined prior-art-ledger block), ARE still registered inside the shared switch with a `prior-art-stage` self-check — so the shared owner's scope is not limited to cross-consumed results, and no principled boundary excludes architecture.

findings.summary: Acceptance #27 and #14 are satisfied only by timing: 28 headers baked into all nine shipped workflow scripts hardcode `.dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/retired-workflow-modules/<name>.js`, a path the rails themselves mandate be gone the moment this work merges. The check passes at the gate and is false one commit later.
findings.evidence: `grep -c "Generated copy of .dev/inprocess" .agents/workflows/*.js` sums to 28 headers across all nine scripts (e.g. architecture.js:11, :35, :542; tdd.js:11, :35, :542, :1180). Contract Acceptance #27 requires "every `Generated copy of` header resolves to an existing file" and #14 requires "Each reference from the nine rails and every workflow script named in Surfaces resolves to an existing repository file". `.agents/skills/rails-run-a-workflow/SKILL.md:228` mandates the opposite state: "Move the run record to `.dev/completed/run-records/` inside the same shipping pull request, before merge. ... Nothing in `.dev/inprocess/` may describe work already merged to `dev` or otherwise shipped." `.agents/skills/rails-read-me/SKILL.md:58` repeats it: "File the run-record inside the shipping PR, before merge". So the committed, merged state can never hold both the headers and the files they name. The contract carries no Decision resolving this: `grep -n "completed/run-records" .dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/contract.md` returns nothing, and contract.md:207 fixes the provenance home at the inprocess path. Worse today: `git ls-files .dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/retired-workflow-modules/` returns 0 — the directory is untracked (`?? .../retired-workflow-modules/` in `git status --short`), so all 28 references already resolve to nothing in git and pass only against this dirty working tree. `.agents/skills/rails-write-a-contract/SKILL.md:55` states the standing bar: "Every item the contract points at — a script, a check, a file — must already exist or be a listed deliverable in the same contract. No dangling references". The supplied hidden-decision stage output raised this as a `severity: high` finding and the contract was not amended.

findings.summary: The run is being gated as finished with three unresolved forced-choice findings standing in its own hidden-decision output — a rails-decisions Violation, and any one confirmed Violation is a FAIL.
findings.evidence: The supplied `hiddenDecisionScan` stage output carries three `findings` (two `severity: high`, one `medium`) — the refute.js stageOutputs trust boundary, the retired-modules header path, and where the six retired analyzer IDs are recorded. `.agents/skills/rails-decisions/SKILL.md:48` states: "**Violation — undecided forced choice.** A choice the work FORCES ... is left unresolved for a tool or implementer to default. No contract advances to IMPLEMENT with an unresolved forced choice." `.agents/skills/rails-run-a-workflow/SKILL.md:72` states: "A forced choice that no approved principle answers stays unresolved for the human. No contract advances past CONTRACT with an unresolved forced choice." None of the three appears in the contract's Decisions: `grep -n "retired-workflow-modules|completed/run-records|AG0012|stageOutputs" .dev/inprocess/2026-09-01-reorganize-rails/contract.md` returns only Surfaces line 490, decision-input line 297, and Acceptance lines 654/658 — no Decision resolving any finding. Timing confirms the scan is the later artifact and was not folded back: `hidden-decision-output-round6.json` mtime Sep 2 18:59 versus `contract.md` mtime Sep 2 18:48. The earlier `hidden-decision-output.json` had `"findings": []`, so these three are new and were never adjudicated. `.agents/skills/rails-decisions/SKILL.md:41`: "**Any one confirmed Violation is a FAIL.**"

findings.summary: A rule whose own text binds workers and adversaries was relocated to `rails-read-me`, the one rail no workflow prompt loads, so the reorganization made it unreachable by the exact roles it governs while leaving the text on disk.
findings.evidence: The rule now lives only at `.agents/skills/rails-read-me/SKILL.md:66`: "**Out-of-repo-root references.** Illegal — workers never add one, adversaries flag any found." (`grep -rn "Out-of-repo-root" .agents/ .dev/reference/` returns that single hit.) `grep -rn "rails-read-me" .agents/workflows/*.js` returns no match (exit 1) — no worker prompt and no adversary prompt in any of the nine scripts loads that file. At HEAD the same rule sat inside the section headed "## Failure-class practice pack (inject into every worker + adversary prompt)" (`git show HEAD:.agents/skills/rails-run-a-workflow/SKILL.md`, line 13 of that section), so it reached every role by construction. The contract's approved `approved-reorganization` decision directs the opposite outcome: "Synchronize the workflow scripts. Audit every `.agents/workflows/*.js` prompt. Keep stage-specific instructions there; load the owning rail for reusable criteria." The Success definition requires that "all workflow prompts and the best-practices guide agree with the owner rails".

findings.summary: The IMPLEMENT worker lost five failure classes it was previously handed: implement.js loads neither rails-decisions nor rails-explorer, and those two rails are now the sole owners of the decision and second-store classes the pack used to inject into every worker.
findings.evidence: `.agents/workflows/implement.js:1281` is the worker's complete rail list: "Read .agents/skills/rails-run-a-workflow/SKILL.md for IMPLEMENT authority, scope, proof, and stop rules. Read .agents/skills/rails-solid-code/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/rails-dry-code/SKILL.md, .agents/skills/rails-real-work/SKILL.md, and .agents/skills/rails-test-code/SKILL.md" — five of nine rails; `rails-decisions` and `rails-explorer` are absent (confirmed by the per-script rail scan: implement.js matches only rails-dry-code, rails-real-work, rails-run-a-workflow, rails-solid-code, rails-test-code). At HEAD, "Unapproved decision", "Undecided forced choice", "Second-store miss", "Status-field lies", and "Byte-space confusion" were all inside "## Failure-class practice pack (inject into every worker + adversary prompt)" in rails-run-a-workflow. Post-change their only homes are `.agents/skills/rails-decisions/SKILL.md:43` and :48, and `.agents/skills/rails-explorer/SKILL.md:59`, :60, :61 — neither file loaded by the worker. The contract's no-loss inventory assigned those destinations, but its `approved-reorganization` decision also requires each prompt to "load the owning rail for reusable criteria", which implement.js does not do for these two owners.

findings.summary: rails-run-a-workflow tells the orchestrator to run `prior-art-ledger.js` as a GROUND script, but ground.js runs the ledger itself from its inlined copied block — prose and executable disagree, and following the prose double-runs the ledger.
findings.evidence: `.agents/skills/rails-run-a-workflow/SKILL.md:63`: "- **Scripts:** `ground.js`, `prior-art-ledger.js` when the change introduces a new capability, and `hidden-decision-scan.js`." The live code takes no such call: `.agents/workflows/ground.js:1387` reads `const ledger = capabilities.length ? await __priorArtLedger({ projectPath, capabilities, ... }) : noCapabilityLedger`, invoking the inlined `prior-art-ledger` copied block (`// ##COPIED-MODULE-BEGIN## prior-art-ledger` at ground.js:1179), and `grep -n "workflow(" .agents/workflows/ground.js` shows every hit is comment prose, never a call. The contract's own `copied-module-convention` states the change: "`prior-art-ledger` is the former standalone prior-art stage, inlined into `ground.js` because chaining it would have consumed the one available nesting level." The contract's `approved-reorganization` requires "workflow schemas must agree with the prose", and the Success definition requires "all workflow prompts and the best-practices guide agree with the owner rails".
